baseline_summary: Required baseline: 8-connected, cost-aware A* on the 1200x800 (N=960k) Nav2 costmap. State = cell index n = x + y*W; edge length l in {r, sqrt(2) r}, r = 0.05 m; corner-cutting forbidden (both orthogonal neighbours must be <= 252). Edge weight in Smac form w = l*(1 + kappa*c/252); the verified Humble sources give equivalent kappa ~4.03 for NavFn (50 + 0.8c per cell, 4-neighbour interpolated potential + gradient-descent path extraction), kappa = 1.0 (Humble default) for Smac 2D (8-neighbour heap A*), and 2.0*Euclid + 1.0*(c/252)^2 with Bresenham LOS for Nav2 Theta*. Heuristic: octile h_oct = r[max(|dx|,|dy|) + (sqrt2-1)min(|dx|,|dy|)], proven admissible and consistent because it is the exact free-grid distance and w >= l; worst-case 8-connected overhead 8.24% (theta = 22.5 deg). Tie-break by lexicographic (f, h). Data structures: float32 g, int32 parent, uint32 generation stamp (no memset), bitset closed, lazy-deletion binary heap; ~12 MB per instance; O((N+E) log N), typical 20-60 ms, worst 150-300 ms, with a connectivity pre-check for unreachable goals. Verified stack facts: nav2_core::GlobalPlanner interface, ComputePathToPose result carries planning_time, IsPathValid returns invalid_pose_indices, default BT replans at 1 Hz, inflation cost = floor(252*exp(-s(d - r_ins))) (inverse d(c) = r_ins - ln(c/252)/s gives clearance without an EDT), Nav2 smoother update y_i += w_d(x_i - y_i) + w_s(y_{i+1} + y_{i-1} - 2y_i) with convergence condition 0 < w_d, w_d + 4 w_s < 2.

proposals.name: TAR-A* (Time-Aware Repairing A*) — C1: stopping-distance speed map, time-domain cost search
proposals.idea: Convert costmap cost to clearance via the analytic inverse of Nav2 inflation, set v_lim = clamp(sqrt(2 a_max d_free), v_floor, v_max) (v_max where c=0), and search with edge cost w_t = l / v_lim [s] and heuristic h_t = h_oct / v_max [s]. Proven admissible/consistent since v_lim <= v_max. Aisle-centering emerges from dynamics parameters (effective multiplier v_max/v_lim: 4.5 at 0.1 m free margin, 1.4 at 1.1 m) instead of an arbitrary cost_travel_multiplier, and the same model feeds travel-time prediction.
proposals.closest_prior_work: Fast Marching Square speed maps (Garrido et al. 2011, RECALLED); Smac Cost-Aware A* (Macenski et al. 2024, VERIFIED); EDF-consistent Lazy Theta* cost (Cobano et al. RAS 2025, VERIFIED).
proposals.expected_gain: Mean clearance +20-40% vs Smac2D kappa=1 with path length within -2..+3%; explainable, physically grounded weights; enables <=15% travel-time prediction error (naive L/v_max is 30-50% off). Planning time p95 <= 100 ms on 960k cells (division replaced by a 256-entry LUT).
proposals.risks: Over-preference for aisle centres lengthening paths (tune v_floor, cost_scaling_factor); discontinuity at the inflation boundary if inflation_radius < r_ins + v_max^2/(2a) (mitigate with R_infl = 1.2 m, s = 2.0, or optional O(N) EDT); DWA's own near-obstacle slowdown must match v_lim for the time metric.
proposals.realtime_budget: Full search p95 <= 100 ms, hard timeout 400 ms (of the 500 ms spec), <= 15 MB per planner instance; 5 robots at 1 Hz full replans <= 0.3 core.

proposals.name: TAR-A* — C2: tube-bounded local repair replanning with bounded fallback
proposals.idea: On each replan, classify the previous path as VALID (return trimmed path, no search), LOCAL (only indices with cost >= 253 are invalid: search from p_{i_a} to p_{i_b} inside a Chebyshev tube of radius rho=3 m painted in a stamp array, accept only if J_new <= (1+eta) J_old + slack, else double rho up to twice) or FULL (global TAR-A*). A drift counter forces a full replan every K=5 repairs or when accumulated cost drift exceeds a threshold, so completeness is preserved and quality drift is bounded relative to the previous path (not to the new global optimum — stated explicitly).
proposals.closest_prior_work: Local Repair A* / WHCA* (Silver 2005, RECALLED); D* Lite and LPA* (Koenig & Likhachev 2002/2004, RECALLED); Sabbadini et al. ICRA 2026 'Revisiting Replanning from Scratch' (VERIFIED) as the counter-hypothesis.
proposals.expected_gain: Replanning p50 <= 5 ms in >= 80% of dynamic-obstacle replans vs 30-80 ms full search; much smaller discrete Frechet distance between consecutive plans (path stability for DWA and fleet prediction); 5-robot replanning CPU ~0.03 core instead of ~0.3.
proposals.risks: Accumulated detours if repairs chain (mitigated by drift reset); no bound vs new global optimum; depends on global_costmap update rate (default 1 Hz would delay obstacle insertion — recommend 5 Hz); benefit may not materialise if from-scratch search is already fast (this is exactly what the D30 benchmark tests).
proposals.realtime_budget: Tube of ~1.4e4 cells for a 6 m invalid segment: ~1-2 ms search plus O(M) validity check; falls back to the 400 ms full-search budget.

proposals.name: TAR-A* — C3: cost-integrated LOS shortcut, clearance-weighted smoothing, curvature/velocity profile and predicted travel time
proposals.idea: (a) String-pulling shortcut accepted only if the supercover segment is collision-free and its time integral int ds/v_lim <= (1+delta)(g_j - g_i), so straightening never worsens time cost or hugs walls; (b) Nav2 gradient smoother plus a clearance term w_c max(0, d_safe - d) grad d using the inflation inverse, with per-iteration rollback on collision/curvature violation; (c) Menger curvature -> v <= omega_max/kappa, forward/backward trapezoidal profile with a_max; (d) T_pred = alpha[ |dtheta_0|/omega_max + sum 2 ds/(v_{i-1}+v_i) + |dtheta_M|/omega_max ], alpha calibrated from logs. Published as amr_msgs/PlanInfo alongside nav_msgs/Path.
proposals.closest_prior_work: A* post-smoothing (Botea 2004 / Nash 2007, RECALLED); APP bidirectional shortcut + perturbation on costmaps (Li & Cheng RA-L 2023, VERIFIED); Dolgov et al. 2010 CG smoothing (RECALLED); Nav2 SimpleSmoother/Smac smoother (VERIFIED source); Pastorelli et al. RA-L 2025 G1 bounded-curvature smoothing (VERIFIED).
proposals.expected_gain: Recovers most of the 8.2% 8-connected length overhead without sacrificing completeness (unlike Theta*'s ~86% success in the 2026 Nav2 benchmark); curvature-feasible paths for the Pure Pursuit/DWA stack; directly delivers the spec's <=15% travel-time prediction metric.
proposals.risks: Shortcut binary search cost O(M log M L/r) on long paths (bounded by the 400 ms budget); smoothing weights must satisfy w_d + 4 w_s < 2; time prediction accuracy depends on the DWA tracking policy and on avoidance stops being excluded from 'actual time' (open question).
proposals.realtime_budget: Post-processing <= 10 ms typical; included in the 400 ms plugin budget; O(M) profile and prediction.

evaluation_plan: Planners via planner_server planner_plugins [AmrAStar, NavFnDijkstra (use_astar=false), NavFnAStar (use_astar=true), Smac2D (kappa 1.0 and 2.0), SmacHybrid (REEDS_SHEPP, min_turning_radius 0.4), ThetaStar] on one shared global_costmap (static+obstacle+inflation, s=2.0, R_infl=1.2 m), tolerance 0.25, called through ComputePathToPose{planner_id}; record result planning_time and in-plugin steady_clock wall time. Datasets: P50 (the spec's 50 seeded start-goal pairs: free cell, cost <= 128, >= 10 m apart), P500 extension, H10 hand-picked hard cases (0.6 m corridor, dead-end aisle, dock approach, diagonal crossing), D30 dynamic-obstacle scenarios (0.3-1.5 m/s crossing workers/forklifts). Metrics mapped to the spec: success rate (>= 98% on P50), planning/replanning time p50/p95/max split by VALID/LOCAL/FULL mode (<= 500 ms), path length, min/mean clearance from an offline EDT of the static map (min >= 0.30 m), smoothness (heading changes > 10 deg, max curvature), predicted-vs-actual travel time over 50 DWA-tracked runs (<= 15%, before/after alpha calibration), consecutive-plan discrete Frechet distance on D30, RSS and 5-robot CPU. Procedure: (1) offline gtest/benchmark harness loading the PGM map into Costmap2D, 3 repetitions, median, determinism check via path hash; (2) online rclpy action-client benchmark over P50/P500 x planners; (3) D30: TAR-A* with LOCAL enabled vs FULL-forced vs Smac2D (optional simple D* Lite control); (4) travel-time calibration and error; (5) ablations: C1 off (kappa=1), C2 off, each C3 term off. CSV logs in logs/planning/ with [timestamp, planner_id, pair_id, success, plan_time_ms, wall_ms, length_m, min_clear_m, mean_clear_m, n_turns, max_curv, T_pred_s, mode, expansions] and [task_id, T_pred, T_actual, err].
implementation_plan: C++17 inside the existing src/amr_navigation ament_cmake package (Python only for benchmark/analysis). Add deps pluginlib, rclcpp_lifecycle, nav2_util, nav_msgs, builtin_interfaces, ament_cmake_gtest. Files: include/amr_navigation/global/{grid_types,speed_map,grid_astar,tube_repair,path_postprocess,amr_astar_planner}.hpp and src/global/*.cpp (ROS-independent core operating on const uint8_t* cost, W, H, res); plugins/global_planner_plugin.xml declaring amr_navigation/AmrAStarPlanner with base nav2_core::GlobalPlanner and CMake pluginlib_export_plugin_description_file(nav2_core ...); config/global_planner.yaml (v_max, a_max, v_floor, omega_max, cost_scaling_factor synced with the costmap, inflation_radius, tube_radius, eta, k_margin, delta_shortcut, w_data, w_smooth, w_clear, d_safe, max_planning_time 0.4, allow_unknown); amr_msgs/msg/PlanInfo.msg (predicted_time, length, min_clearance, mode, expansions, plan_time_ms) published by the plugin next to the nav_msgs/Path returned from createPlan (costmap mutex locked for the search, as Smac does). Tests (gtest, target >= 70% coverage): speed-map inverse/monotonicity, A* cost equality vs Dijkstra on random grids, numerical heuristic-consistency check, corner-cut prohibition, determinism, timeout; tube repair bound and fallback; shortcut collision-free and cost-non-worsening, smoother convergence condition, profile acceleration constraints, synthetic-path time prediction; plugin lifecycle test with a synthetic Costmap2DROS. Benchmark: benchmark/{bench_planners.py, pairs_50.yaml, analyze.py}; docs/algorithms/astar.md condensed from the brief. Nav2 integration: keep the default 1 Hz replanning BT (plugin decides VALID/LOCAL/FULL) or the replan-only-if-path-invalid BT; recommend global_costmap update_frequency 5 Hz. Schedule: week 1 core A* + speed map + unit tests; week 2 plugin + NavFn/Smac benchmark pipeline; week 3 C3 post-processing + time prediction; week 4 C2 repair + D30 + ablations; week 5 report and tuning. Compute budget: full search p95 <= 100 ms, LOCAL p50 <= 5 ms, hard timeout 400 ms returning an empty path to BT recovery, <= 15 MB per instance, 5-robot replanning <= 0.3 core even if all replans are FULL.
open_questions: Final warehouse map aisle-width distribution (number/length of 0.6 m corridors) drives inflation_radius, cost_scaling_factor and v_floor tuning.
Should the global costmap be the full 1200x800 map at 5 Hz update (vs the 1 Hz default) so dynamic obstacles reach the global planner within the 500 ms replanning budget; CPU impact to be measured.
Does the DWA team's near-obstacle slowdown policy match the stopping-distance v_lim used in C1? This is the precondition for the <=15% travel-time prediction target.
Definition of 'actual travel time' for the 15% metric (docking excluded? avoidance stops included?) must be agreed with the reporting team.
Should amr_perception's TrackedObstacle predicted footprints be injected as a global costmap layer (would raise the LOCAL-repair share)?
Should a hook for fleet lane reservations (extra_cost[N] added to w_t) be opened now, ahead of the corridor-graph phase-2 option?

arXiv export API returned HTTP 429 for every call (WebFetch and host curl); the survey used the arXiv search UI, /abs pages, GitHub Humble sources and venue pages instead. Numbers quoted from search summaries (e.g. Smac 38% faster than NavFn) should be re-checked in the full texts before appearing in the final report.
